p01.why: An alias cannot be combined with another type specifier such as unsigned.

p02.why: f(Int) and f(int) are one function, so it is defined twice.

p03.why: Block-scope aliases of aliases name int, and main returns 0.

p04.why: An alias cannot be declared again as a member of the same class, even for the same type.

p05.why: Deleted functions can use an incomplete class as parameter and return type.

p06.why: Outside a class, an alias can be declared again for the same type in either form.

p07.why: An alias denotes the same type.

p08.why: A function-type alias can declare (not define) a function, and an array alias declares a char[4].

p09.why: A class key cannot refer to an enumeration.

p10.why: struct Tag in a parameter list declares Tag in the enclosing namespace, so all uses name one class.

p11.why: A pointer to a forward-declared class is valid, and the class is complete before use.

p12.why: const has no effect on reference and function aliases and goes to the elements of an array alias.

p13.why: struct Node in the return type declares Node at namespace scope, which the later definition completes.

p14.why: The specifier inside namespace n declares n::Hidden, a different incomplete class, so p->v is invalid and &h does not convert.

p15.why: The function that needs the size is defined after the class is complete.

p16.why: A class key cannot be used with the name of a type alias.

p17.why: Forward declarations after the definition are valid, and class and struct name the same class.

p18.why: A typedef must declare a name.

p19.why: The block alias hides the global one; qualified names reach the others.

p20.why: I is used outside the block that declares it.

p21.why: An opaque enumeration with a fixed type can be defined later with the same base.

p22.why: struct Later in a member declaration declares Later in the enclosing namespace, so it is the same class as the later definition.

p23.why: An unnamed C-like class gets the typedef name for linkage.

p25.why: An alias declared again in a class for a different type.

p26.why: enum class cannot be used in a reference to an enumeration.

p27.why: An alias declaration can define an unnamed class.

p28.why: An object of an incomplete class cannot be created.

p29.why: Outer does not declare a nested class Missing.

p30.why: An unscoped enumeration without a body needs a fixed underlying type.

p31.why: struct stat finds the class even though a function has the same name.

p32.why: Member access on an incomplete class.

p33.why: The opaque declaration fixes the type, so the conversion works before the definition; the value is 7.

p34.why: An alias declared again for a different type.

p35.why: An alias cannot have a storage class.

p36.why: A function definition with an incomplete return type.

p37.why: enum E used before E is declared.

p38.why: The enumeration is declared again with a different underlying type.

p39.why: Pointers, references and function declarations need only a declaration.

p40.why: A member typedef changes the meaning of I after a use; GCC rejects, Clang and EDG accept (Q-0066).

p41.why: The alias name T is reused for a class that it does not name.

p42.why: An alias cannot have the name of a variable in the same scope.

p43.why: class and struct can refer to the same class.

p44.why: A qualified name that lookup does not find.

p45.why: An alias cannot have an initializer.

p46.why: The unnamed class with a member function uses a typedef name for linkage; GCC 14 accepts, GCC 16, Clang and EDG reject (Q-0067).

p47.why: union used for a class that was declared with struct.

p48.why: A typedef can declare several names, each with its own declarator.

p49.why: An alias can name an incomplete class, and the object is made after the definition.

p50.why: A declaration of only a class key and a qualified name; GCC accepts, Clang and EDG reject (Q-0093).

p51.why: const on an alias of a pointer applies to the pointer and repeats harmlessly.

p52.why: An opaque scoped enumeration has underlying type int, so its size is known.

p53.why: enum E refers to the declared enumeration.

p54.why: A function definition with a parameter of incomplete class type.

p55.why: Local is declared in the block of f and used outside it.

p56.why: The enumeration is declared again with a different scope.

p57.why: A later data member changes the meaning of the function name f; GCC rejects, Clang and EDG accept (Q-0066).

p58.why: A typedef can give a class its own name, and the alias can be declared again for the same type.

p59.why: A nested class can be declared in its class and defined outside.

p60.why: Member aliases have class scope and are reached with S::.

p61.why: A function-type alias cannot be used to define a function.
